_comment: ElevenLabs Conversational AI — tool configuration. `slot claude voice agent-config` substitutes {{BASE_URL}} with the live Tailscale Funnel URL and writes the X-Flowslot-Token static header from FLOWSLOT_BRIDGE_HMAC_SECRET. `slot claude voice agent-push` PATCHes these directly to the live agent via the ElevenLabs API. v2.15+: one agent talks to MANY slots on the same host — every per-slot tool requires a `slot` field.

tools.name: list_slots
tools.description: List slots on this host with status (tmux session alive, git branch, container counts, last activity). ALWAYS call this first if you don't yet know which slot the user means, or whenever focus is ambiguous. Cheap and cached for 10 seconds.

tools.name: get_claude_state
tools.description: Return a structured snapshot of what Claude is doing on a specific slot right now. Use when the user asks about STATE (how's it going, is Claude stuck, what's it working on, is it done). Fast call; prefer over get_claude_last_output for status. If `tmux_alive` is false, no Claude session is running for that slot — suggest `slot claude --slot <name>`. IMPORTANT: if `bootstrapping: true` (the slot has no recorded events yet — usually because it was just created), DO NOT report 'idle/no response/Claude hasn't replied' from this tool alone. Read `output_tail` (multi-line buffer) on the same response, or call get_claude_last_output to see what's actually on screen — last_claude_preview is a single line and is misleading in this state.

bootstrapping.description: True when no events exist for this slot yet (fresh-created or hooks not firing). Read output_tail or call get_claude_last_output.

output_tail.description: Multi-line tmux scrollback. Populated only when bootstrapping=true.

tools.name: get_claude_last_output
tools.description: Return raw text from Claude's terminal on a specific slot (last N lines). Use ONLY when the user asks to READ or HEAR what Claude actually said word-for-word. Speak the returned text VERBATIM — do not paraphrase, do not summarize. For status, use get_claude_state instead. Returns 404 if no session for that slot.

lines.description: Number of terminal lines to capture. 30 for short replies, 100+ for long output.

tools.name: inject_message
tools.description: Send a message into a specific slot's Claude REPL as if the user typed it. Default urgent=false queues the message (Claude picks it up when its current tool finishes). urgent=true sends Escape first to interrupt Claude's current action, then the message. Use urgent only when the user clearly wants to stop Claude's current work. Returns 404 if the slot has no live Claude session — surface that and suggest `slot claude --slot <name>`.

text.description: What to type into Claude's REPL.

urgent.description: If true, interrupt Claude first (Escape), then send.

tools.name: watch_for_stop
tools.description: Long-poll: block until Claude's next turn ends (Stop event) on a specific slot, or about 22 seconds elapse. Use when the user says 'let me know when it's done' or wants to wait on the call until Claude finishes. Server caps the wait at ~22s and returns `still_working: true` if Claude didn't stop in time — this is NORMAL, not an error. When you see still_working=true, briefly tell the user 'still working' and call watch_for_stop again to keep waiting. Returns 404 if slot has no session.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait before giving up (1-300).

still_working.description: True when the 22s cap hit before Claude stopped. Call watch_for_stop again to keep waiting.

tools.name: get_system_status
tools.description: Host + bridge + all-slots overview in one cheap call. Use when the user asks about server health, load, disk, or wants a global "what's running" view. Slots section is summary-only (use list_slots for full per-slot detail).

tools.name: create_slot
tools.description: Create a new slot on this host AND start Claude on it in one shot (clones the repo, copies HQ .env files, runs docker compose up, launches Claude in a tmux session). TWO-CALL: first call with confirm=false returns the dry-run plan (port_base, branch, repo_url, remote_path). Read the plan back to the user. Only call again with confirm=true after the user explicitly confirms. On success, response includes claude_started=true — the slot is ready to receive inject_message immediately, no separate start_claude_on_slot call needed. If claude_started=false (rare — Claude failed to launch), the slot is still created and usable; tell the user and offer to retry via start_claude_on_slot. 409 means the slot name already exists — say so and stop.

branch.description: Git branch to check out. Defaults to the slot name.

confirm.description: false = dry-run plan; true = actually create.

tools.name: start_claude_on_slot
tools.description: Start a Claude Code session on an existing slot in a detached tmux session. RECOVERY TOOL: create_slot already starts Claude automatically, so you almost never need this for fresh slots. Use it when (a) Claude crashed on an older slot, (b) the user explicitly says 'start Claude on <slot>', or (c) create_slot returned claude_started=false. Idempotent and not destructive: if Claude is already running on that slot, returns started=false with reason='already running' — mention that to the user. No confirmation needed. Model defaults to whichever Claude model is most-used on this host (typically opus); pass `model` to override.

model.description: Optional model alias ('opus','sonnet','haiku') or full id. Defaults to host's most-used Claude model.

tools.name: restart_claude_on_slot
tools.description: Kill the existing Claude tmux session on a slot and start a fresh one. TWO-CALL: first call with confirm=false returns the slot's current state (tmux_alive, status, elapsed_seconds). If Claude is mid-activity, WARN the user explicitly: 'Claude has been thinking for 40 seconds — restarting drops that. Sure?' Only call again with confirm=true after the user agrees. Model defaults to host's most-used.

model.description: Optional model alias or full id.

confirm.description: false = return current state for read-back; true = actually restart.

tools.name: destroy_slot
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE — wipes a slot completely (kills Claude tmux, `docker compose down -v --remove-orphans`, rm -rf the slot dir). TWO-CALL: first call with confirm=false returns the destruction plan (containers_count, dir_size_mb, last_event). Read it back: 'Destroying <slot> removes <N> containers, <size> MB, and stops Claude. Confirm?' Require an explicit verbal 'yes' or 'destroy <slot>' from the user. Only then call again with confirm=true. 404 means already gone — say so and stop.

confirm.description: false = dry-run plan; true = actually destroy.
